title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-06-24
source: center lodge, mics mounted on rails->120-min. Sony cassette audience master-> analog cassette XL II, no dolby->Sony TC D5M DAT->playback on Sony PCM R-700-> HDD via za2->CDR master via CD Architect->EAC->Sound Forge->SHN

ai_review.summary: Clear audience tape captures a legendary Dark Star and St. Stephen performance.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this late‑June ’70 audience recording, calling it one of the finest Ken‑Mark‑Jim tapes and praising the powerful Dark Star, St. Stephen and Easy Wind stretches. The sound quality is consistently described as good for an audience source, with no major flaws noted, making the show both sonically enjoyable and musically unforgettable.

ai_rating.rationale: All six reviews are highly positive (4‑5 stars) and highlight standout performances; recording is praised as good for an audience source, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape lauded as clear and well‑balanced for its era; no significant dropouts or muffling mentioned. Reviewers note the rarity of soundboard tapes from this period but consider this audience source excellent.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers describe the set as a ‘truly special, powerful, awesome’ performance with seamless flow, especially highlighting the Dark Star/​St. Stephen segment.

band_member_comments.Phil: Multiple reviewers note Phil Lesh 'banging away' and delivering unreal bass lines on NFA/Easy Wind.
